output.question: Has USAA announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. USAA has publicly confirmed multiple rounds of layoffs: the most recent directly verified announcement opened here was reported on April 10, 2024, when the company said it was cutting approximately 220 positions across multiple offices. Earlier, on May 17, 2023, USAA confirmed the elimination of approximately 300 roles; that report said the 2023 total had exceeded 900 eliminated employees. A later 2024 report also says USAA confirmed a second round of cuts that year, but the company did not disclose the number affected.

key_facts.fact: USAA announced approximately 220 layoffs in April 2024, affecting employees across multiple offices, including remote workers.
USAA confirmed a second round of layoffs in 2024, but its spokesman declined to disclose how many workers were affected or where they worked.
USAA confirmed the elimination of approximately 300 roles in May 2023, across most offices and different functions.
The May 2023 report said the 300-role round brought USAA's 2023 eliminated-employee total to just over 900.

passages.quote: USAA has announced another round of layoffs, which are the first for 2024 after the company laid off nearly a thousand roles across different departments in 2023. The San Antonio-based insurance and banking giant said in a statement to MySA Wednesday that the company made the difficult decision to cut around 220 positions within USAA.
USAA confirmed that it has laid off a second round of employees this year, five months after the company laid off 220 people.
After careful consideration, we made the difficult decision to eliminate approximately 300 roles across most of our offices and different functions.

caveats: The sources opened in this run are contemporaneous news reports quoting USAA spokespeople, not a standalone USAA press release.
The number of employees affected by the later 2024 round was not disclosed.
This research does not establish whether USAA announced additional layoffs after the verified 2024 reports; no later primary-source announcement was opened and verified here.
